To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is considerable development across the middle and secondary school years in the accuracy of text consistency judgments, particularly for adequate readers in those text integration tasks that maintain local coherence; and (2) accuracy in text consistency judgment is related to reading comprehension, particularly for adolescent comprehenders who are performing well on comprehension tasks.

there was considerable growth in text integration skills among adequate comprehenders across the middle and secondary grades, and accuracy in text consistency tasks accounted for significant variance in comprehension, particularly for those students who were adequate comprehenders.

(a) the development of the ability to integrate local information into a coherent whole continues through adolescence, particularly among adequate comprehenders; (b) struggling comprehenders have difficulty integrating local information into a larger coherent whole, and (c) the ability to integrate text information is related to reading comprehension, particularly among adequate readers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the development of text comprehension is influenced by the ability to integrate local and global information.
the role of text integration processes in reading comprehension, with a focus on how adolescents’ text integration skills develop across grades 6 to 12.
the development and role of inferential processing during reading.

the results of this study suggest that text consistency judgments, and the processes that underlie them, are important for comprehension and that there is considerable developmental change across the middle and early high school years.
text consistency judgments are important for reading comprehension, but they are not the most important.

the findings of this study suggest that text consistency judgments may be an important component of text processing and comprehension, and that they are particularly sensitive to the demands of reading comprehension in the adolescent years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of inferential processing in the middle school years is characterized by a shift from a focus on local text consistency to a focus on the maintenance of local coherence.
there is considerable developmental growth across adolescence for the ability to maintain local coherence, particularly for adequate readers.
text consistency judgments are important for reading comprehension, and that struggling readers need to develop these processes to improve their comprehension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
text integration processes are malleable across the middle and secondary years, and that text consistency judgments may be a useful tool to assess these processes.

text integration processes, as measured by text consistency judgments, continue to develop throughout middle and high school, with the greatest gains occurring for those with adequate reading comprehension skills.
text integration processes are not fixed by the end of middle school.
